I will keep all 12 mu in cotton this year. I have been growing cotton for 40 years, my land is not large, and with only two people in the household I want a management plan that is steady, familiar, and practical for the labor I have. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on a moderate water schedule instead of gambling on rainfall. Since my education level is high and I know the value of stable performance, I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed, but I will avoid pushing inputs too hard because on 12 mu I care more about reliable output and cost control than chasing the highest possible yield. I will use plough tillage at the start of the season because I want a clean seedbed and good root development. For fertilizer, I will apply a balanced but cotton-focused program with nitrogen as the main driver, enough phosphorus for establishment, and a moderate potassium rate to support boll development. I will also plan several pesticide sprays because cotton in this area usually needs active pest control if I want stable production. My goal is a solid, manageable crop with dependable yield rather than an aggressive, high-risk plan.
